purpose: Phase 4 freeze manifest for Corpus V1 - the bounded/resumable full local crawl of uettaxila.edu.pk run entirely locally (--dry-run, zero Convex/Gemini/Pinecone/Neon calls) per the mandate's Phase 3 architecture. This manifest is the reproducibility record for the frozen corpus directory; the corpus payload itself (documents.jsonl, raw/) is not committed to git, matching this repo's existing manifest-not-payload convention.
corpusLocation: /mnt/d/uetgpt_corpus_v1 (D: drive, chosen for available disk space; all existing files made read-only at freeze time via chmod -R a-w - verified 0 writable files among documents.jsonl, raw-manifest.jsonl, and all 2456 raw/ files. Directory entries themselves remain writable: this is a DrvFs/WSL Windows-mount limitation, not a chmod scope gap - new files could still be added to the tree, though no existing content can be silently overwritten in place.)

crawlRun.note: Wall-clock span includes an extended web.uettaxila.edu.pk outage (roughly 2026-08-21 06:20 to 2026-08-22 12:35 UTC per session logs) during which the crawl was intentionally backed off rather than hammering a downed origin; active crawl time was substantially less than the wall-clock span.

crawlerInvocation.geminiCallsGuarantee: config-level: pdf.describeImages=false, html.describeImages=false, independent of any GEMINI_API_KEY* present in .env.local
crawlerInvocation.cloudCallsVerified: 0 Convex/Pinecone/Gemini calls - grepped for convex.cloud/pinecone/generativelanguage.googleapis/gemini across every crawl console log this session; zero matches

knownDisclosedGaps: 1 duplicate documentId (f373f18e2166e26cf1aa9d90420414e94ff2e7628af06f89ec26ae9748dbc960): https://web.uettaxila.edu.pk/ and https://web.uettaxila.edu.pk/UETsub/examination/examViewDtSregS.asp?frm_cate=Date%20Sheet%20BSc both canonicalize to the site root; crawled ~4 hours apart during the outage window, near-identical content (same wordCount, differing contentHash - likely dynamic page content). Not a code defect; two entries sharing a documentId with matching content are trivially collapsible if a downstream consumer needs strict dedup.

362 failed_fetch_terminal + 32 failed_extract URLs represent real, permanent gaps (mostly the extended site outage's aftermath - persistently-500ing backend endpoints like departmentfaculty?departmentId=N, plus a handful of genuinely low-quality/unextractable PDFs). These will not resolve on further crawling of the same run; a future crawl against a healthier origin may recover some of them.
bugsFoundAndFixedThisSession: DeadLetterQueue.add() never reported dead-lettering back to callers, so the ledger row for a permanently-failed URL stayed non-terminal forever (scripts/crawler.py)
failed_extract was missing from TERMINAL_STATES despite being definitionally final (scripts/uet_crawler/crawl_ledger.py)

begin_run()'s exhaustive computation used max_depth (normally finite, unrelated) instead of max_pages, making FRONTIER_EXHAUSTED unreachable for any depth-bounded exhaustive crawl (scripts/crawler.py)

amendments.scopeExplicitlyLimited: This is a source-file-only edit. The live Pinecone index (44,792 vectors, uetgpt-corpus-v1-qwen1024) and any local Convex copy were NOT touched - a full removal (deleting the corresponding vectors) was considered and explicitly deferred: the chunk-level file (embeddings/all_chunks.jsonl) links chunks to documents via a Convex-internal document id that does not match documents.jsonl's hash-based documentId in any static file checked, and this project's own established constraint is that Pinecone deletes must be by exact id only, never by metadata filter (delete-by-filter was measured unreliable in earlier work). Deleting without a verified id mapping was assessed as unsafe. This means Corpus V1 as actually embedded/upserted (44,792 vectors) is UNCHANGED and remains exactly what every certified number in this evaluation (Recall@10=0.98, HitRate@5, MRR, the golden-set's fee-discrepancy finding in report.md §9) was measured against. This edit only affects what a FUTURE re-embed/rebuild of the corpus would include.
amendments.otherYearlyReissuedFamiliesFoundButNotTo: A broader scan for year-numbered document families found several that superficially resemble the Prospectus pattern but are historical-record series, not reissued editions, and were deliberately left alone: IEEE_branch_YYYY_Annual_Report.pdf (2013-2025, 9 editions), Course Allocation Spring YYYY, Curriculum-YYYY.pdf, Entrepreneurship-YYYY.pdf, CPDCalendarYYYYUETTaxila.pdf, CPED-Fall-YYYY.pdf, 'Annual Report Cover Pages(YYYY-YYYY).pdf', FinalYearProjectsfor-YYYY-Session.pdf. Each year's record documents something that actually happened that year rather than superseding the prior year's content, so removing older ones would destroy real information rather than save redundant storage - not a match for the user's stated 'latest-year-only' policy, which was specifically about documents that get reissued with the same role each cycle (the Prospectus being the clear example).
